category_title: Adolescents positioned as struggling readers who resist institutional labels
scenario_title: Standardized test preparation in remedial reading class
minimal_context: Angelica is in her reading class practicing for a standardized test by reading past passages and answering multiple-choice questions.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Today we are going to read passages from past standardized tests and answer the multiple choice questions. The goal is making sure we go back to the passage to find the answers.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Great, it's another reading class. I really didn't like to read as much because it would be really boring and stuff.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: We need to practice this for an hour every single day. Please go ahead and start reading the first passage.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Every year since third grade I've been in a reading class and I had to read for like an hour every single day. I'm just really bored with it.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Just try to get through it. Look at the first question and see what you think.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Circles an answer quickly) I would read the stories and I wouldn't pay attention to the stories. And I would read the questions and I would, just from what I remembered, I would pick the answer. And I would never go back to the story.

task.content: Read passages from past standardized tests and answer multiple choice questions
task.learning_goal: Making sure we go back to the passage when we take the [state standardized] test

context.materials: Passages from past standardized tests, multiple choice questions, sticky notes, notebooks
context.social_setting: Classroom setting with teacher and partner share
context.time_context: For an hour every single day

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: The design of these tests—that stripped her of agency to choose what, when, and how she read
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: I would read the stories and I wouldn't pay attention to the stories. And I would read the questions and I would, just from what I remembered, I would pick the answer. And I would never go back to the story.
